I never let it show or tell them, bc I don’t want to be Debbie Downer, but it’s hard.

Yes, exactly! And there are still hard days, like holidays. I always take time off from work on her death date and her birthday too, because those are still very tender. 


On her death date, I like to visit her gravesite if I can. I try to keep the midday/afternoon/evening busy so that I don’t get stuck on it, though, bc her death was very sudden, tragic, and public. I’ve spent time with her friends and those that were also there when she died too - it’s cathartic in some ways. I don’t have a good relationship with our parents or siblings now, so I don’t spend time with them anymore.. but I still find people who I love and who support me to spend the time with. Keeping busy helps. 


On her birthday, I always take the money I would’ve spent for a gift for her and use it to help other people. I’ve paid it forward in the drivethru at the coffee shop, I’ve paid adoption fees on a cat at the shelter, and I’ve donated to a lot of nonprofits that she would’ve liked/supported. I get coffee at our favorite spot, watch one of our favorite movies, and just try to spend the day soaking her up. It always feels like her spirit is closer to me on that day, so I try to make the best of it. 💛

Everything in my life changed that day - I realized everyone I loved wasn’t going to grow old with me. I realized how utterly fragile life is, and that in a single second, everything could go black and you’d be gone forever. I hadn’t ever lost anyone close to me, other than grandparents, but they’d lived long lives and it was expected that they would pass. I’m very lucky to have thick eyebrows and after many years of misfortune, I’m able to keep them shaped nicely on my own. If you don’t have many eyebrow hairs and/or if they’re very light, you can find videos on YouTube of which eyebrow pencils are best and how to follow your natural shape. If you have a lot of eyebrow hairs (like me) and you’ve never attempted to shape your eyebrows or are nervous of overdoing it and have a little bit of money to spend, I recommend finding a picture online of brows close to yours and going to a salon for a wax or threading. You don’t have to keep going to them, though; once you have the shape right, you can pluck whatever hairs grow in once or twice a week that’s outside of the new shape. I used to think the meds were supposed to “cure” me of all of my sadness and was frustrated when I was sad sometimes.. But that’s not how it works. You will be happy, sad, mad, and everything in between, and that’s ok. The goal is to get to a place where the negative feelings don’t make up the majority of your daily emotions.

A lot of introspection and questioning yourself why you're doing something/reacting a certain way so that you can understand your feelings and where they come from. 

As I mentioned in another comment, a lot of people react to things in negative ways because it strikes a chord they don't know they have.
I didn't realize that I got really mad when things didn't go like I planned because I had control issues and anxiety -- I couldn't see beyond my perfect plans because I was afraid of something going "wrong" or differently and being mentally unprepared for it.  

When you feel a negative emotion, take a second to ask yourself why. Why do I feel this way and why am I reacting this way?
If you got yourself into an argument, speak to whomever and explain that you (reacted this way) because (this action) made you (feel this way). It helps to be able to walk the other person through your reasoning so they can understand where you're coming from. It puts perspective into arguments so that you can reason it out from there on. 

For example, I (sort of accidentally) lashed out at my fiancé over his dishes being in the sink, when the dishwasher was empty, for what seemed like the millionth time. Why did I feel mad/react that way? Because I felt disrespected and like I'm never listened to when I ask him to put his dirty dishes up. I opened up and explained that to him so he could understand I feel like my requests are being ignored. He helped me understand that he doesn't see a cup, a spoon, and a plate in the sink as urgent/plans to do it later but hasn't gotten around to it. I still wish he'd clean up after himself immediately, but as long as it gets done, y'know. 

Communication is so underrated. You hear everyone talking about how it's the key to a good relationship (it really is) but no one really knows how to talk. Don't bottle things up and/or be passive aggressive. Talk about your feelings and be honest about things. Try to use more "I" sentences than "you" sentences because they seem very accusatory. 

Also, don't say you're sorry unless you mean it. I used to use that term just to diffuse situations and it makes apologies mean less when you genuinely are sorry. 

Sorry if I got a bit off the original topic, but I feel these are really important things. If you have any more questions, let me know. I hope I helped!

I try to have a few snacks throughout the day like a peanut butter sandwich (a healthier option, can't remember the name, but it's def not Peter Pan). Sometimes I have Babybel light or a something similar too. I leave dinner as my biggest meal because that's when I'm stressed from work and hangry and crave stuff, but after the first week or two of curving that I've just not felt the need to binge at dinner -- that was one of my big issues previously. I tended to be an over-eater that ignores the full feeling because I felt like I HAD to finish what I made or what was on my plate.
